commits.summary: Adds hideKeyboard + scrollUntilVisible(direction UP, timeout 30000, visibilityPercentage 40, centerElement true) before the extendedWaitUntil MARKER assert.
commits.reason: Its own successor commit (21b2bf92) documents that hideKeyboard ABORTS the Expo Go flow ('the composer has no standard dismiss action'), so this commit ships a step proven to fail the flow. The scrollUntilVisible step is part of the exact tap/scroll family the closure flags as the un-root-caused recurrence risk.

commits.summary: Replaces hideKeyboard with tapOn 'Live chat' (title tap to dismiss keyboard); keeps scrollUntilVisible centerElement true.
commits.reason: This is the commit the closure record itself names: not-reproduced.json source_comparison.failed_cont_candidate == this SHA ('Adds a tap on the Live chat title and scrollUntilVisible for MARKER ... causation_claimed: false'). It failed the CONT run, and its successor documents the title tap left the keyboard up.

commits.summary: Replaces the title tap with tapOn point '50%, 30%' + waitForAnimationToEnd 3000ms, and flips centerElement true -> false.
commits.reason: The closure record explicitly calls this tip 'unverified': 'Replaces the title tap with an unverified 50%,30% coordinate tap'. A blind coordinate tap is layout/simulator-resolution-dependent. Decisive fact: the verified no-repro evidence (cycle-2 2026-09-29T16:22:38Z and cycle-3 2026-09-29T16:29:42Z, real devices, iOS light+dark) ran this flow WITHOUT any tap/wait/scroll steps and passed with actual_native_failures=0. No evidence exists that any of these steps are needed; the reuse_limit clause additionally requires this file to hash 276cdcf5 on the consuming base, which only main's bytes satisfy.

recurrence_risk.note: All three commits add or mutate exactly the flagged tap/wait/scrollUntilVisible family (closure open_flags[0]: 'If a future flow re-adds similar scroll/wait steps it can recur with nothing on file explaining it'). The only configuration verified against real services is main's YAML, which contains none of these steps. If a future ORI-CONT-004 cycle hits a genuine keyboard/visibility failure, the remedy must be a fresh, separately-reviewed change with its own disposition - not a resurrection of these commits.
